title: Uniform excess under a minorized transition
statement: Let $V$ be a finite nonempty set, let $P:V\times V\to\mathbb{Q}$ have each column sum equal to $1$, and suppose $P(u,v)\ge\delta$ for every $u,v\in V$, where $\delta\in\mathbb{Q}$. Let $p:V\to\mathbb{Q}$ have sum $1$. For a function $q:V\to\mathbb{Q}$, define its uniform excess to be $\max_{v\in V}(q(v)-1/|V|)$. Then the uniform excess of $v\mapsto\sum_{u\in V}p(u)P(u,v)$ is at most $(1-|V|\delta)$ times the uniform excess of $p$.
